```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(hmmTMB))

## Paths work both from the project root (tar_make) and from quarto_reports/ (manual render).
root_path  <- if (dir.exists("_targets")) "." else ".."
store_path <- file.path(root_path, "_targets")
r_path     <- file.path(root_path, "r")

## season_info() labels the forecast season; hindcast_auc() scores the Mutze spot check.
source(file.path(r_path, "a_season_info.R"))
source(file.path(r_path, "d_score_plague_hindcast.R"))
source(file.path(r_path, "d_build_risk_grid_newdata.R"))

tar_load(
  c(
    fit_zones_sf, aus_shp, grdc_subregion_adj,
    hmm_data, plague_hmm, plague_hmm_unsupervised, plague_hmm_ppc, plague_hmm_pseudores,
    plague_risk_map_supervised, plague_risk_map_unsupervised,
    plague_risk_map_uncertainty_supervised, plague_risk_map_uncertainty_unsupervised,
    plague_risk_map_nowcast_supervised, plague_risk_map_nowcast_unsupervised,
    yearly_plague_occurrence, recent_plague_maps, recent_plague_maps_map, mutze_plague_maps,
    rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, gpp_rolling_raster_6, soil_moisture_anomaly_raster, min_temp_raster_coarse,
    gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast, soil_moisture_anomaly_raster_nowcast,
    gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_12, gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3, min_temp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3,
    prediction_region_sf,
    plague_hindcast_supervised, plague_hindcast_unsupervised,
    plague_hindcast_scores_supervised, plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised
  ),
  store = store_path
)

## The two models compared throughout: with and without the plague anchors (the unsupervised exit
## formula omits the soil-group terms, which it can't identify without anchors).
model_variants <- list(
  Supervised   = list(hmm = plague_hmm, risk_map = plague_risk_map_supervised,
                      risk_map_uncertainty = plague_risk_map_uncertainty_supervised,
                      risk_map_nowcast = plague_risk_map_nowcast_supervised),
  Unsupervised = list(hmm = plague_hmm_unsupervised, risk_map = plague_risk_map_unsupervised,
                      risk_map_uncertainty = plague_risk_map_uncertainty_unsupervised,
                      risk_map_nowcast = plague_risk_map_nowcast_unsupervised)
)
model_colours <- c(Supervised = "#2166ac", Unsupervised = "#8c8c8c")

## Hazard palette for risk (calm sage to brick red), shared with the project's other risk outputs.
hazard_colors <- c("#3F5B45", "#7C8C43", "#C99A34", "#BE5F2C", "#7A2626")

## Map layers in WGS84: national outline, fitted AE zones, and GRDC subregions clipped to those zones.
aus_sf <- st_as_sf(aus_shp) |> st_transform(4326)
fit_zones_ll <- st_transform(fit_zones_sf, 4326)
zones_bbox <- st_bbox(fit_zones_ll)
s2_was_on <- sf::sf_use_s2()
suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE))
grdc_subregion_ll <- st_transform(grdc_subregion_adj, 4326) |>
  sf::st_intersection(sf::st_union(fit_zones_ll)) |>
  suppressMessages() |>
  suppressWarnings()
suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(s2_was_on))

## The four chew-card streams share every coefficient, so chewcard_count stands in for all four.
chewcard_streams <- c("chewcard_count", "chewcard_block2", "chewcard_block3", "chewcard_block4")

## AE zones (transitions) and adjusted AE zones (burrow/chew-card zone effects).
zone_levels <- levels(hmm_data$ae_zone)
adj_zone_levels <- levels(hmm_data$ae_zone_adj)

## Mann-Whitney AUC: probability a positive case outranks a negative one.
auc_fn <- function(yes, no) {
  r <- rank(c(yes, no))
  (sum(r[seq_along(yes)]) - length(yes) * (length(yes) + 1) / 2) / (length(yes) * length(no))
}

## One-season-ahead risk shown as a map tile layer, used by every risk/uncertainty panel.
risk_tile_map <- function(df, fill_col, title, fill_scale) {
  xr <- range(df$x); yr <- range(df$y); pad <- 0.6
  ggplot() +
    # geom_raster fills the regular 0.1 degree grid without the hairline gaps geom_tile leaves between rows.
    geom_raster(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = .data[[fill_col]])) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    fill_scale +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1] - pad, xr[2] + pad), ylim = c(yr[1] - pad, yr[2] + pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
}

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
#| include: false

## Numbers quoted in the Summary, computed here so the Summary can come first.

## Panel size.
n_rows     <- nrow(hmm_data)
n_paddocks <- n_distinct(hmm_data$ID)
fit_states <- sort(unique(hmm_data$aus_state))

## Anchors.
n_plague    <- sum(hmm_data$state == 2, na.rm = TRUE)
n_nonplague <- sum(hmm_data$state == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
mapped_seasons <- recent_plague_maps |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(season, year) |>
  arrange(year, match(season, c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring")))
first_mapped_year <- min(mapped_seasons$year)

## Forecast period: the latest period shared by the time-varying transition covariates, and the season after it.
latest_shared_period <- function(rasters) {
  periods <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(rasters, names))
  key <- as.integer(sub(".*_", "", periods)) * 100 + as.integer(sub("_.*", "", periods))
  periods[which.max(key)]
}
period_seasons <- function(period) {
  info <- season_info(as.Date(paste(sub(".*_", "", period), sub("_.*", "", period), "15", sep = "-")))
  season_order <- c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring")
  cov_season <- as.character(info$season)
  target <- season_order[(match(cov_season, season_order) %% 4) + 1]
  list(period = period, covariate_season = cov_season, covariate_year = info$year_adj,
       target_season = target, target_year = if (target == "Summer") info$year_adj + 1 else info$year_adj)
}
forecast <- period_seasons(latest_shared_period(list(rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_12, gpp_rolling_raster_6,
                                                     min_temp_raster_coarse, gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3, soil_moisture_anomaly_raster,
                                                     min_temp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3)))
nowcast  <- period_seasons(latest_shared_period(list(rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_12, gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast,
                                                     min_temp_raster_coarse, gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3, soil_moisture_anomaly_raster_nowcast,
                                                     min_temp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3)))

## Current risk by AE zone, for both models: mean, 90th percentile and maximum across each zone's cells.
zone_raster <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(fit_zones_ll), plague_risk_map_supervised, field = "ae_zone")
risk_by_zone <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  z <- terra::zonal(m$risk_map, zone_raster,
                    fun = function(x, ...) c(mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), q90 = stats::quantile(x, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
                                             max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, ae_zone = as.character(z[[1]]), mean = z[[2]][, 1], q90 = z[[2]][, 2], max = z[[2]][, 3])
})
top_zones <- risk_by_zone |> filter(Model == "Supervised") |> arrange(desc(mean)) |> slice_head(n = 2)

## Hindcast skill (state-mean summary), both models.
hindcast_scores <- bind_rows(
  mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_supervised$scores, Model = "Supervised"),
  mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised$scores, Model = "Unsupervised")
) |>
  filter(stat == "mean")
get_hindcast <- function(model, predictor_name, era_name, col = "auc_within") {
  hindcast_scores[[col]][hindcast_scores$Model == model & hindcast_scores$predictor == predictor_name & hindcast_scores$era == era_name]
}
fmt2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)

## Residual calibration and posterior-predictive statistics outside the simulated range.
pr_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(plague_hmm_pseudores, function(x, nm) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  tibble::tibble(Stream = nm, n = length(x), Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x), `% |z|>2` = 100 * mean(abs(x) > 2))
})
ppc_summary <- plague_hmm_ppc$simulated |>
  group_by(statistic) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(simulated), sim_lo = quantile(simulated, 0.025), sim_hi = quantile(simulated, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(plague_hmm_ppc$observed, by = "statistic") |>
  mutate(inside = observed >= sim_lo & observed <= sim_hi)
ppc_outside <- ppc_summary$statistic[!ppc_summary$inside]
ppc_label <- function(stat) {
  stream <- c(trap_count = "trap", burrow_count = "burrow", chewcard_count = "chew-card")[sub(":.*", "", stat)]
  what <- sub(".*: ", "", stat)
  what <- dplyr::recode(what, mean = "mean", SD = "SD", `Pr(0)` = "share of zeros", `Pr(10)` = "share of fully chewed sessions")
  paste(stream, what)
}
## "a, b and c" for lists in the text.
and_join <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
chew_freq_stats <- c("chewcard_count: Pr(0)", "chewcard_count: Pr(10)")
chew_freq_ok <- chew_freq_stats[!chew_freq_stats %in% ppc_outside]

## Decoded-state agreement and second-state shares.
decoded <- lapply(model_variants, function(m) m$hmm$viterbi())
agreement_pct <- round(100 * mean(decoded$Supervised == decoded$Unsupervised), 1)
state2_share <- sapply(decoded, function(v) mean(v == 2))
```

## Summary

- **Model.** A two-state (not-plague / plague) hidden Markov model fitted to `r format(n_rows, big.mark = ",")` paddock-seasons across `r n_paddocks` paddocks in `r length(fit_states)` states. Live-trap, active-burrow and chew-card surveys are the observations; rainfall whiplash, GPP, soil-moisture anomaly and minimum temperature drive the seasonal transitions into and out of plague.
- **Anchoring.** `r format(n_plague, big.mark = ",")` paddock-seasons are anchored to plague and `r format(n_nonplague, big.mark = ",")` to not-plague, from `r nrow(mapped_seasons)` hand-mapped plague seasons since `r first_mapped_year`.
- **Current forecast.** For `r forecast$target_season` `r forecast$target_year` (from `r forecast$covariate_season` `r forecast$covariate_year` covariates), onset risk is highest in `r top_zones$ae_zone[1]` (zone mean `r scales::percent(top_zones$mean[1], accuracy = 0.1)`) and `r top_zones$ae_zone[2]` (`r scales::percent(top_zones$mean[2], accuracy = 0.1)`).
- **Early warning.** On recorded plague years before 2013, which the model never saw, one-year-ahead onset risk has a within-state AUC of `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast"))`, against `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "rain_whiplash", "hindcast"))` for rainfall whiplash alone (same-year onset `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast"))`).
- **Model checks.** Randomised residuals are calibrated for every stream (means `r fmt2(min(pr_summary$Mean))` to `r fmt2(max(pr_summary$Mean))`, SDs `r fmt2(min(pr_summary$SD))` to `r fmt2(max(pr_summary$SD))`). `r if (length(ppc_outside) > 0) paste0("Data simulated from the model match the real data except for the ", and_join(ppc_label(ppc_outside)), ", which fall just outside the simulated 95% ranges.") else "Data simulated from the model match every checked statistic."`
- **Supervised vs. unsupervised.** The two models agree on `r agreement_pct`% of decoded states. Without anchors the second state is rarer (`r scales::percent(state2_share[["Unsupervised"]], accuracy = 0.1)` against `r scales::percent(state2_share[["Supervised"]], accuracy = 0.1)` of paddock-seasons) and more extreme.
- **Main limitations.** The plague transition rests on few independent mapped plague seasons; the forecast reaches one season ahead only; and validation before 2013 relies on coarse state-by-year plague records.

## Data

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data

## Surveys per state: paddocks, paddock-seasons, and paddock-seasons with each observation stream.
hmm_data |>
  group_by(State = aus_state) |>
  summarise(Paddocks = n_distinct(ID), `Paddock-seasons` = n(),
            `Live-trap` = sum(!is.na(trap_count)), `Active burrow` = sum(!is.na(burrow_count)),
            `Chew card` = sum(!is.na(chewcard_count)), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(Paddocks)) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = -State) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Paddock-seasons surveyed by", columns = c(`Live-trap`, `Active burrow`, `Chew card`)) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

Each paddock is one time series of seasons, from `r min(hmm_data$year_adj)` to `r max(hmm_data$year_adj)`; seasons without a survey stay in the panel with no observations, so the hidden state is carried through them by the transition model. Repeat visits within a season are reduced to the first visit. The fit covers `r length(zone_levels)` agro-ecological (AE) zones; `"Qld Central"` is excluded, having no surveys since 2008 and no plague anchors.

The burrow and chew-card zone effects use `r length(adj_zone_levels)` adjusted AE zones, merging AE zones with few surveys so every zone has enough data in each state (`r/a_adjust_aez.R`); the transitions keep all `r length(zone_levels)` original AE zones.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-obs-zones

## Which AE zones make up each adjusted AE zone, and the burrow/chew-card surveys behind each.
hmm_data |>
  group_by(`Adjusted AE zone` = ae_zone_adj) |>
  summarise(`AE zones` = paste(sort(unique(as.character(ae_zone))), collapse = ", "),
            `Burrow surveys` = sum(!is.na(burrow_count)), `Chew-card surveys` = sum(!is.na(chewcard_count)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

The northern adjusted zones split the two northern AE zones at the NSW/Queensland border.

## Anchoring

Known plague occurrence fixes the hidden state where it is known. Plague extents are hand-digitised for each mapped season (`raw_data/plague_occurrence/recent_plague_maps/`). From the start of the census (Summer 2013) to the latest mapped season, a paddock-season inside a mapped extent is anchored to plague. Outside the mapped extents, a paddock-season is anchored to not-plague only in seasons with no plague mapped anywhere in Australia; in seasons with a mapped plague, the model estimates the state of every paddock outside the extents, since hand-drawn extents say least about absence while a plague is under way. The two seasons before a paddock's plague anchor are also left unanchored, because a plague is rarely confirmed the season it begins. Full rule: `r/c_anchor_plague_state.R`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-anchor-maps
#| fig-cap: "The hand-digitised plague extents used as anchors, one panel per mapped season."
#| out-width: "100%"

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root_path, recent_plague_maps_map))
```

`r format(n_plague, big.mark = ",")` paddock-seasons are anchored to plague and `r format(n_nonplague, big.mark = ",")` to not-plague (`r round(100 * (n_plague + n_nonplague) / n_rows, 1)`% of the panel). Each plague anchor is a separate paddock falling inside a mapped extent, but they come from only `r nrow(mapped_seasons)` mapped seasons (`r paste(paste(mapped_seasons$season, mapped_seasons$year), collapse = ", ")`), so the plague transition is estimated from a modest number of independent plague events. Before `r first_mapped_year` there are no anchors.

```{r}
#| label: fig-anchor-vs-model
#| fig-cap: "Share of anchored paddock-seasons in plague (points, where anchors exist) against each model's mean smoothed Pr(plague state) across all paddocks in that state and season (lines)."
#| fig-asp: 0.55

## Smoothed state probabilities are in hmm_data's row order; season mid-months give a date axis.
season_mid_month <- c(Summer = 1L, Autumn = 4L, Winter = 7L, Spring = 10L)
anchor_vs_model <- hmm_data |>
  mutate(
    Supervised   = plague_hmm$state_probs()[, "state2"],
    Unsupervised = plague_hmm_unsupervised$state_probs()[, "state2"],
    anchored     = case_when(state == 2 ~ 1, state == 1 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    date         = as.Date(paste(year_adj, season_mid_month[as.character(season)], "15", sep = "-"))
  ) |>
  group_by(aus_state, date) |>
  summarise(anchored_share = mean(anchored, na.rm = TRUE), Supervised = mean(Supervised),
            Unsupervised = mean(Unsupervised), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(anchor_vs_model, aes(date)) +
  geom_line(data = pivot_longer(anchor_vs_model, c(Supervised, Unsupervised), names_to = "Model"),
            aes(y = value, colour = Model), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = anchored_share), colour = hazard_colors[5], size = 1.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~aus_state, ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = model_colours, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(plague state)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The supervised model follows the anchors where they exist, as it must. The unsupervised model, fitted without them, still rises through the mapped plague seasons, so the observation data carry much of the same signal.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spec

tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Specification,
  "States", "2 (not-plague, plague), one time series per paddock; stationary initial distribution",
  "Transitions", "Pr(enter plague) ~ rainfall whiplash (with a zone-varying random slope) + 12-month GPP anomaly + 6-month GPP + minimum temperature + AE-zone random intercept. Pr(leave plague) ~ rainfall whiplash x soil group + 3-month GPP anomaly + soil-moisture anomaly x soil group + soil group + 3-month minimum-temperature anomaly + minimum temperature + AE-zone random intercept (the unsupervised model omits the soil-group terms). Minimum temperature and 6-month GPP are levels, centred and scaled; the rest are anomalies. This season's covariates set the transition to next season's state.",
  "trap_count", "Total captures per session (trap success). Negative binomial (mean, shape); mean ~ season + season x cropping system (sorghum / winter cereal regions) + crop group (all tied) + log trap-nights (offset, coefficient fixed at 1).",
  "burrow_count", "Active burrows per session. Negative binomial (mean, shape); mean ~ season + season x cropping system (sorghum / winter cereal regions) + fine-scale GPP + crop group + crop stage + soil type (all tied) + adjusted AE zone (per state) + log metres searched (offset).",
  "chewcard_count (+3 blocks)", "Cards chewed out of 10, in up to four blocks of 10 cards. Beta-binomial (prob, overdispersion sigma); prob ~ season + crop group + crop stage + soil type (all tied) + adjusted AE zone (per state); every coefficient shared by the four blocks."
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::cols_width(Component ~ px(170))
```

- **Tied** terms have one shared value in both states: they describe how easily mice are detected (season, crop, soil, search conditions), which should not depend on whether a paddock is in plague. The state intercepts and the adjusted-zone effects differ between states, carrying the difference in mouse numbers.
- **Families.** Trap and burrow counts use the negative binomial; chew cards use the beta-binomial, which lets the chew rate vary between sessions so cards within a session tend to be chewed together. The beta-binomial is not in CRAN hmmTMB; it comes from the patched build pinned in `renv.lock`.
- **Effort.** Search effort (trap-nights, metres searched) enters as an offset, so means are per unit of effort.
- Full specification, and the alternatives tested: `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`.

### Transition hypotheses

The candidate drivers of each transition, with the mechanism behind each and how it is measured. Every window is a trailing window ending at the current season, since this season's covariates set the transition to next season's state. Rainfall, GPP, soil-moisture and temperature measures are anomalies against each cell's own climatology for that time of year, so "wet" or "cold" means unusual for that place rather than an absolute amount. Terms marked \* may vary spatially (by zone or soil group). "In model" is read from the fitted transition formula.

```{r}
#| label: hypothesis-tables-prep

## Variables in the supervised model's formula for each transition ([1, 2] entering, [2, 1] leaving).
transition_formulas <- plague_hmm$hid()$formula()
enter_vars <- all.vars(stats::as.formula(transition_formulas[1, 2]))
leave_vars <- all.vars(stats::as.formula(transition_formulas[2, 1]))

## One hypothesis table: "Model term" lists the variables in that transition's formula matching each
## row's variable pattern (a regular expression over that hypothesis's candidate measures).
hypothesis_table <- function(tbl, title, model_vars) {
  tbl |>
    mutate(`Model term` = vapply(pattern, function(pt) {
      matched <- if (is.na(pt)) character(0) else grep(pt, model_vars, value = TRUE)
      if (length(matched) == 0) "--" else paste0("`", matched, "`", collapse = ", ")
    }, character(1))) |>
    select(Covariate, Mechanism, Measurement, `Model term`) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Model term`) |>
    gt::tab_header(title = title) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
    gt::cols_width(Covariate ~ px(150), Mechanism ~ px(320), `Model term` ~ px(150))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hypotheses-enter

tibble::tribble(
  ~Covariate, ~Mechanism, ~Measurement, ~pattern,

  "Long-term rainfall anomaly*", "Consistently good seasons build populations gradually; in some regions sustained conditions may matter more than a single swing. Likely nonlinear (thresholds).", "24, 36 and 48-month rolling anomaly; a smooth for the best window", "^rain_rolling(24|36|48)_anomaly$",
  "Long-term GPP anomaly", "Proxy for crop yield (food amount and quality); consistent food lets populations build over time.", "12, 24, 36 and 48-month rolling anomaly", "^gpp",
  "Soil-moisture anomaly (current)*", "Burrowing capacity: decides whether good food conditions translate into population growth.", "Current-season (3-month) anomaly", "^soil_moisture_anomaly$",
  "Soil-moisture anomaly (long-term)*", "Persistently good or poor burrowing conditions promote or suppress populations.", "12 and 24-month rolling anomaly", "^soil_moisture_rolling(12|24)_anomaly$",
  "Minimum temperature", "If it does not get cold, breeding may not pause; what matters is whether cold conditions occurred, not when.", "3, 6 and 12-month rolling anomaly; number of unusually cold months (anomaly below -1 SD) in the last 12", "^min_temp",
  "Time since last plague", "Populations may need time to recover after a crash before another plague is possible.", "Needs a post-plague state or a semi-Markov structure rather than a covariate; not yet included", NA
) |>
  hypothesis_table("Entering a plague", enter_vars)
```

```{r}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Covariate, ~Mechanism, ~Measurement, ~pattern,
  "Rainfall whiplash", "The conditions that caused the plague have ended; the current-season whiplash falls as conditions revert.", "Current whiplash (as for entry)", "^rain_whiplash",
  "Minimum temperature", "Cold conditions stress mice and stop breeding.", "3 and 6-month rolling anomaly; number of unusually cold months in the last 6", "^min_temp",
```

## Estimates

### Transitions

```{r}
#| label: fit-stats

fit_stats_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  fs <- attr(m$hmm, "fit_stats")
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, Convergence = m$hmm$out()$convergence, AIC = fs$aic, `Fit attempts` = fs$attempts)
})
```

Both models converged (`r paste(paste0(fit_stats_tbl$Model, ": AIC ", format(round(fit_stats_tbl$AIC, 1), big.mark = ",")), collapse = "; ")`). Their AICs are not comparable with each other, because the supervised model's likelihood is conditioned on the anchors.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coeff

## Fixed-effect transition coefficients (logit scale), both models side by side.
purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  cf <- m$hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, Parameter = rownames(cf), Estimate = cf[, 1])
}) |>
  mutate(Transition = ifelse(grepl("^S1>S2", Parameter), "Enter plague", "Leave plague"),
         Term = sub("^S[12]>S[12]\\.", "", Parameter)) |>
  select(-Parameter) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Transition, Model), values_from = Estimate, names_sep = " | ") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = -Term, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Transition fixed effects (logit scale)",
                 subtitle = "Rainfall whiplash is the pooled slope; zone deviations are below")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-zone-effects

## Zone random effects: intercept deviations and total rainfall-whiplash slopes, by model and transition.
zone_effects <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  re <- m$hmm$hid()$coeff_re()
  fe <- m$hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
  rn <- rownames(re)
  is_slope <- grepl(":rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak\\.[0-9]+$", rn)
  tibble::tibble(
    Model      = label,
    Transition = ifelse(grepl("^S1>S2", rn), "Enter", "Leave"),
    ae_zone    = zone_levels[as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", rn))],
    Effect     = ifelse(is_slope, "Whiplash slope", "Intercept deviation"),
    value      = re[, 1]
  ) |>
    mutate(value = ifelse(Effect == "Whiplash slope",
                          value + fe[paste0(ifelse(Transition == "Enter", "S1>S2", "S2>S1"), ".rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak"), 1],
                          value))
})

sup_enter_slopes <- zone_effects$value[zone_effects$Model == "Supervised" & zone_effects$Effect == "Whiplash slope" & zone_effects$Transition == "Enter"]

zone_effects |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Effect, Transition, Model), values_from = value, names_sep = " | ") |>
  rename(`AE zone` = ae_zone) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = -`AE zone`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.72em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "AE-zone effects on the transitions (logit scale)",
                 subtitle = "Intercept deviations from the pooled intercept, and each zone's total rainfall-whiplash slope")
```

The zone effects are random effects, so thinly surveyed zones are shrunk towards the pooled estimate rather than estimated on their own. Supervised intercept deviations span `r fmt2(min(zone_effects$value[zone_effects$Model == "Supervised" & zone_effects$Effect == "Intercept deviation"]))` to `r fmt2(max(zone_effects$value[zone_effects$Model == "Supervised" & zone_effects$Effect == "Intercept deviation"]))`, and the entering-plague whiplash slope is positive in `r sum(sup_enter_slopes > 0)` of `r length(sup_enter_slopes)` zones (`r fmt2(min(sup_enter_slopes))` to `r fmt2(max(sup_enter_slopes))`).

### Covariate effects

```{r}
#| label: covariate-effects-data

## Numeric transition covariates in either model (read from the fitted formulas); soil group, a
## factor, is held at its most common level.
numeric_covariates <- setdiff(unique(unlist(lapply(model_variants, function(m) transition_covariates(m$hmm)))), "soil_group")
covariate_labels <- c(rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak = "Rainfall whiplash", gpp_anomaly = "GPP anomaly (12-month)",
                      gpp_rolling6 = "GPP (6-month)", min_temp = "Minimum temperature",
                      gpp_rolling3_anomaly = "GPP anomaly (3-month)", soil_moisture_anomaly = "Soil-moisture anomaly",
                      min_temp_rolling3_anomaly = "Min-temp anomaly (3-month)")[numeric_covariates]
covariate_medians <- sapply(numeric_covariates, function(cv) median(hmm_data[[cv]], na.rm = TRUE))
common_soil_group <- names(which.max(table(hmm_data$soil_group)))

## Variables in a model's formula for one transition, so a covariate is only shown where it enters.
transition_vars <- function(hmm, entering) {
  f <- hmm$hid()$formula()[if (entering) 1 else 2, if (entering) 2 else 1]
  all.vars(stats::as.formula(f))
}

## Placeholder values for every observation-formula covariate (they don't affect transition predictions).
fill_obs_placeholders <- function(nd, hmm) {
  obs_data <- hmm$obs()$data()
  obs_vars <- unique(unlist(lapply(hmm$obs()$formulas(), function(p) unlist(lapply(p, function(s) unlist(lapply(s, all.vars)))))))
  for (v in setdiff(obs_vars, names(nd))) {
    nd[[v]] <- if (is.factor(obs_data[[v]])) factor(levels(obs_data[[v]])[1], levels = levels(obs_data[[v]])) else mean(obs_data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  nd
}

## Each covariate varied over its 5th-95th percentile with the others at their median, in every AE
## zone.
covariate_effects_by_zone <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(numeric_covariates, function(cv) {
    seq_vals <- seq(quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 50)
    purrr::map_dfr(zone_levels, function(zn) {
      nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(covariate_medians, each = length(seq_vals)), nrow = length(seq_vals),
                                 dimnames = list(NULL, numeric_covariates)))
      nd[[cv]] <- seq_vals
      nd$soil_group <- factor(common_soil_group, levels = levels(hmm_data$soil_group))
      nd$season <- factor("Spring", levels = c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring"), ordered = TRUE)
      nd$ae_zone <- factor(zn, levels = zone_levels)
      nd <- fill_obs_placeholders(nd, m$hmm)
      tpm <- m$hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = nd)
      tibble::tibble(Model = label, covariate = cv, ae_zone = zn, value = rep(seq_vals, 2),
                     transition = rep(c("Entering plague", "Leaving plague"), each = length(seq_vals)),
                     probability = c(tpm["state 1", "state 2", ], tpm["state 2", "state 1", ])) |>
        ## Only the transition(s) this covariate actually enters.
        filter((transition == "Entering plague" & cv %in% transition_vars(m$hmm, TRUE)) |
               (transition == "Leaving plague" & cv %in% transition_vars(m$hmm, FALSE)))
    })
  })
})

## Summarised per model as the mean across zones and the range between zones.
covariate_effects <- covariate_effects_by_zone |>
  group_by(Model, covariate, transition, value) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(probability), lo = min(probability), hi = max(probability), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-covariate-effects
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Transition probabilities as each covariate varies over its 5th-95th percentile, others held at their median and soil group at its most common level (", common_soil_group, "). Only the transition(s) a covariate enters are shown. Lines show the mean across AE zones and bands the range between zones, supervised and unsupervised models together.")
#| fig-asp: 0.7

ggplot(covariate_effects, aes(value, mean, colour = Model, fill = Model)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(transition ~ covariate_label, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = model_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = model_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability per season") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-whiplash-by-zone
#| fig-cap: "Pr(entering plague) as rainfall whiplash varies over its 5th-95th percentile in each AE zone (its zone-varying random slope on entry), other covariates held at their median."
#| fig-asp: 0.5

covariate_effects_by_zone |>
  filter(covariate == "rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak", transition == "Entering plague") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, probability, colour = ae_zone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(transition ~ Model, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "turbo", name = "AE zone") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = covariate_labels[["rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak"]], y = "Probability per season") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: exit-by-soil-data

## Supervised model's Pr(leaving plague) as exit whiplash and the soil-moisture anomaly vary, in each
## soil group (their soil-group interactions), other covariates at their median, averaged over zones.
exit_soil_covariates <- intersect(c("rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak", "soil_moisture_anomaly"), transition_vars(plague_hmm, FALSE))
exit_by_soil <- purrr::map_dfr(exit_soil_covariates, function(cv) {
  seq_vals <- seq(quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 50)
  purrr::map_dfr(levels(hmm_data$soil_group), function(sg) {
    purrr::map_dfr(zone_levels, function(zn) {
      nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(covariate_medians, each = length(seq_vals)), nrow = length(seq_vals),
                                 dimnames = list(NULL, numeric_covariates)))
      nd[[cv]] <- seq_vals
      nd$soil_group <- factor(sg, levels = levels(hmm_data$soil_group))
      nd$season <- factor("Spring", levels = c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring"), ordered = TRUE)
      nd$ae_zone <- factor(zn, levels = zone_levels)
      nd <- fill_obs_placeholders(nd, plague_hmm)
      tpm <- plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = nd)
      tibble::tibble(covariate = cv, soil_group = sg, ae_zone = zn, value = seq_vals, probability = tpm["state 2", "state 1", ])
    })
  })
}) |>
  group_by(covariate, soil_group, value) |>
  summarise(probability = mean(probability), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(covariate_label = covariate_labels[covariate])

## Direction of each model's pooled entry whiplash slope, for the text below.
entry_whiplash_sign <- vapply(model_variants, function(m) sign(m$hmm$coeff_fe()$hid["S1>S2.rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak", 1]), numeric(1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-exit-by-soil
#| fig-cap: "Supervised model: Pr(leaving plague) as rainfall whiplash and the soil-moisture anomaly vary over their 5th-95th percentile, by soil group (their soil-group interactions on exit), other covariates at their median, averaged over AE zones."
#| fig-asp: 0.45

ggplot(exit_by_soil, aes(value, probability, colour = soil_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("cracking clay" = "#8c510a", "duplex/calcareous loam" = "#d8b365", "sandy earth" = "#5ab4ac"), name = "Soil group") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(leaving plague) per season") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

In both models, state 2 is the high-activity state (higher trap, burrow and chew-card levels; @tbl-obspar), so the curves describe the same kind of transition. Without anchors, the second state is rarer and more extreme, so the unsupervised model's entry probabilities read as "entering high activity" rather than the mapped plague definition. The pooled rainfall-whiplash slope on entry is `r if (length(unique(entry_whiplash_sign)) == 1) paste(if (entry_whiplash_sign[1] > 0) "positive" else "negative", "in both models") else "of opposite sign in the two models"`: `r if (entry_whiplash_sign[["Supervised"]] > 0) "a sharp swing from dry to wet raises the chance of entering plague" else "a sharp swing from dry to wet lowers the chance of entering plague"` in the supervised model.

### Observation model

```{r}
#| label: tbl-obspar

## Observation parameters at the first row of hmm_data (a snapshot: means and probabilities also
## vary with season, effort, crop and zone), both models.
purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  p <- m$hmm$obs()$par(t = 1)[, , 1]
  keep <- !grepl(paste(chewcard_streams[-1], collapse = "|"), rownames(p)) & !grepl("size", rownames(p))
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, Parameter = rownames(p)[keep], `State 1` = p[keep, 1], `State 2` = p[keep, 2])
}) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = c(`State 1`, `State 2`), names_sep = " | ") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = -Parameter, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Observation parameters by state (one snapshot)")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-season-effects
#| fig-cap: "Supervised model: fitted trap mean, burrow mean and chew-card probability by season and state, at otherwise fixed conditions. The season effect is shared by both states, so the lines differ in level but not in shape."
#| fig-asp: 0.4

season_rows <- sapply(levels(hmm_data$season), function(s) which(hmm_data$season == s)[1])
par_by_season <- plague_hmm$obs()$par(t = season_rows)
season_effects <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(season_rows), function(i) {
  tibble::tibble(season = names(season_rows)[i],
                 stream = rep(c("Trap mean", "Burrow mean", "Chew-card probability"), each = 2),
                 state  = rep(c("State 1", "State 2"), 3),
                 value  = c(par_by_season["trap_count.mean", , i], par_by_season["burrow_count.mean", , i],
                            par_by_season["chewcard_count.prob", , i]))
})

ggplot(season_effects, aes(factor(season, levels = names(season_rows)), value, colour = state, group = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~stream, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`State 1` = "#2166ac", `State 2` = hazard_colors[5]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fitted value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Model checks

### Residuals

```{r}
#| label: tbl-residuals

pr_summary |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(Mean, SD, `% |z|>2`), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = n) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Randomised quantile pseudo-residuals, supervised model")
```

Randomised quantile residuals (`r/d_randomised_pseudores.R`) compare each observation with the model's one-season-ahead forecast of it; for a well-specified model they are standard normal (mean 0, SD 1, about 5% beyond ±2). hmmTMB's built-in version is biased for count data, so it is not used.

### Simulated data

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-cap: "100 datasets simulated from the supervised model (grey), against the real value (red), for summary statistics of each stream. Simulated values are computed over the same surveyed paddock-seasons as the real data."
#| fig-asp: 0.8

ggplot(plague_hmm_ppc$simulated, aes(simulated)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey75", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(data = plague_hmm_ppc$observed, aes(xintercept = observed), colour = hazard_colors[5], linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~statistic, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Simulated datasets") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: ppc-text

ppc_line <- function(s) {
  r <- ppc_summary[ppc_summary$statistic == s, ]
  sprintf("%s real %.3f, simulated 95%% range %.3f-%.3f", tools::toTitleCase(ppc_label(s)), r$observed, r$sim_lo, r$sim_hi)
}
```

- **Chew cards.** `r ppc_line("chewcard_count: Pr(0)")`; `r ppc_line("chewcard_count: Pr(10)")`. `r if (length(chew_freq_ok) == 2) "Both lie inside the simulated ranges: the beta-binomial reproduces sessions where cards are chewed together." else if (length(chew_freq_ok) == 1) paste0("The ", ppc_label(chew_freq_ok), " is reproduced; the other lies just outside its simulated range.") else "Both lie outside the simulated ranges."`
- **Traps and burrows.** `r if (length(grep("trap|burrow", ppc_outside)) > 0) paste0("Outside the simulated range: ", paste(sapply(grep("trap|burrow", ppc_outside, value = TRUE), ppc_line), collapse = "; "), ". The negative binomial does not fully capture how trap and burrow counts cluster, although the residuals are calibrated row by row.") else "All trap and burrow statistics lie inside the simulated ranges."`

## Forecast skill

### Hindcast against recorded plague years

```{r}
#| label: hindcast-prep

hindcast_first <- plague_hindcast_supervised |>
  filter(!is.na(onset)) |>
  distinct(year_adj, season) |>
  arrange(year_adj, match(season, c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring"))) |>
  slice(1)
hindcast_n         <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast", "n")
hindcast_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast", "n_flagged")
anchored_n         <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "anchored era", "n")
anchored_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "anchored era", "n_flagged")
```

Before 2013 there are no anchors and almost no surveys, so plague years recorded by state in `yearly_plague_occurrence.csv` are labels the model never saw. The hindcast (`r/d_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R`) runs the transition model over every grain-zone grid cell from `r hindcast_first$season` `r hindcast_first$year_adj`, giving each cell's **onset** risk, Pr(not-plague → plague), and **occupancy**, Pr(plague), carried forward season to season through the transitions. Each state's cells are averaged, and the highest season in each year is scored against that state-year's record (`r/d_score_plague_hindcast.R`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hindcast-scores

hindcast_scores |>
  filter(!(Model == "Unsupervised" & predictor == "rain_whiplash")) |>
  mutate(Model = ifelse(predictor == "rain_whiplash", "(covariate only)", Model),
         Predictor = recode(predictor, occupancy = "Occupancy", onset = "Onset, same year",
                            onset_lead = "Onset, one year ahead", rain_whiplash = "Rainfall whiplash alone"),
         Era = factor(recode(era, hindcast = "Before 2013 (unanchored)", `anchored era` = "2013 onwards (anchored)"),
                      levels = c("Before 2013 (unanchored)", "2013 onwards (anchored)")),
         `Within-state AUC (95% interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", auc_within, auc_within_lcl, auc_within_ucl),
         `Pooled AUC` = sprintf("%.2f", auc)) |>
  arrange(Era, Predictor, Model) |>
  select(Era, Predictor, Model, `Within-state AUC (95% interval)`, `Pooled AUC`) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Era") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Hindcast skill against recorded plague state-years",
                 subtitle = "Intervals resample whole years")
```

- **Within-state AUC is the main score**: flagged and unflagged years compared within the same state, so differences in baseline risk between states don't count.
- **Before 2013** (`r hindcast_n_flagged` flagged of `r hindcast_n` state-years), one-year-ahead onset scores `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast"))` (supervised) and `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast"))` (unsupervised), against `r fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "rain_whiplash", "hindcast"))` for rainfall whiplash alone.
- **From 2013** only `r anchored_n_flagged` of `r anchored_n` state-years are flagged, too few to separate the models; these years are anchored in the supervised model but not in the unsupervised one.
- **Caveats.** The records are coarse (a whole state, a calendar year, no WA), and the rainfall-whiplash definition was chosen partly against the same records, so its score and the models' use of it are not fully blind.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hindcast-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "State-mean onset risk (highest season each year), with recorded plague years shaded. Dashed line: start of anchoring (2013)."
#| fig-height: 7

hindcast_series <- bind_rows(
  mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_supervised$state_year, Model = "Supervised"),
  mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised$state_year, Model = "Unsupervised")
)
flagged_years <- distinct(filter(hindcast_series, flag == 1), state, year_adj)

ggplot(hindcast_series, aes(year_adj, onset_mean, colour = Model)) +
  geom_rect(data = flagged_years, aes(xmin = year_adj - 0.5, xmax = year_adj + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2012.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~state, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = model_colours, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(not-plague → plague), state mean") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: mutze-1984

## Spot check against Mutze's (1989) mapped 1984 SA plague extent: do SA cells inside it get higher
## 1984 onset risk than SA cells outside it?
mutze_1984 <- sf::st_union(sf::st_make_valid(filter(mutze_plague_maps, year == 1984)))
sa_outline <- filter(aus_shp, ST_NAME == "SA")
mutze_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(list(Supervised = plague_hindcast_supervised, Unsupervised = plague_hindcast_unsupervised), function(h, model) {
  cells <- h |>
    filter(year_adj == 1984, !is.na(onset)) |>
    group_by(cell, x, y) |>
    summarise(onset = max(onset), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(cells) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(cells, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = sf::st_crs(aus_shp))
  in_sa <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sa_outline)) > 0
  inside <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sf::st_transform(mutze_1984, sf::st_crs(pts)))) > 0
  d <- cells[in_sa, ]
  d$inside <- inside[in_sa]
  tibble::tibble(Model = model, n_inside = sum(d$inside), onset_inside = mean(d$onset[d$inside]),
                 onset_outside = mean(d$onset[!d$inside]), auc = hindcast_auc(d$onset, as.integer(d$inside)))
})
mutze_text <- if (nrow(mutze_check) > 0) {
  paste0("**Mapped 1984 SA plague (Mutze 1989).** ", mutze_check$n_inside[1],
         " SA grain cells fall inside the mapped extent; their 1984 onset risk averages ",
         sprintf("%.3f", mutze_check$onset_inside[1]), " against ", sprintf("%.3f", mutze_check$onset_outside[1]),
         " elsewhere in SA (supervised), a cell-level AUC of ", fmt2(mutze_check$auc[1]),
         " (unsupervised ", fmt2(mutze_check$auc[2]), "). One mapped extent, so a spot check rather than a skill score.")
} else {
  "**Mapped 1984 SA plague (Mutze 1989)** falls before the first hindcast season."
}
```

`r mutze_text`

### Onset skill at paddock level

```{r}
#| label: onset-skill

## For each paddock-season not anchored to plague, does predicted Pr(enter plague) separate paddocks
## whose next season is anchored plague from those anchored not-plague? (The same anchors the
## supervised model was fitted to, so a consistency check rather than an out-of-sample test.)
eligible_by_model <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  p_enter <- m$hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = hmm_data)["state 1", "state 2", ]
  hmm_data |>
    mutate(p_enter = p_enter) |>
    arrange(ID, season_year_adj) |>
    group_by(ID) |>
    mutate(next_state = lead(state)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is.na(next_state), is.na(state) | state != 2)
})

onset_skill <- purrr::imap_dfr(eligible_by_model, function(eligible, label) {
  yes <- eligible$p_enter[eligible$next_state == 2]
  no  <- eligible$p_enter[eligible$next_state == 1]
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, `Onsets` = length(yes), `Stayed clear` = length(no),
                 `Median Pr(enter) before onset` = median(yes), `Median Pr(enter) before staying clear` = median(no),
                 AUC = auc_fn(yes, no))
})

onset_skill |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(Onsets, `Stayed clear`)) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("Median"), decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = AUC, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

```{r}
#| label: operational-threshold

## The risk cutoff that best separates onsets from non-onsets (Youden's J), supervised model.
sup_eligible <- eligible_by_model$Supervised
roc_points <- purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(sup_eligible$p_enter)), function(th) {
  high <- sup_eligible$p_enter >= th
  onset <- sup_eligible$next_state == 2
  tibble::tibble(threshold = th, sensitivity = mean(high[onset]), specificity = mean(!high[!onset]))
})
best_threshold <- roc_points |>
  mutate(youden = sensitivity + specificity - 1) |>
  slice_max(youden, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
risk_values_sup <- terra::values(plague_risk_map_supervised)
pct_map_above <- 100 * mean(risk_values_sup[!is.na(risk_values_sup)] >= best_threshold$threshold)
```

A cutoff of **`r scales::percent(best_threshold$threshold, accuracy = 0.1)`** best separates onsets from non-onsets in the supervised model, catching `r scales::percent(best_threshold$sensitivity, accuracy = 1)` of onsets while clearing `r scales::percent(best_threshold$specificity, accuracy = 1)` of seasons that stayed clear. `r round(pct_map_above, 1)`% of the current risk map (@fig-risk-map) is at or above it. It is a rough guide to where "elevated" starts on this model's scale, not an operational rule.

### Supervised vs. unsupervised

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-comparison

tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c("Paddock-seasons decoded in state 2", "Decoded-state agreement between models",
              "Hindcast before 2013: onset, same year", "Hindcast before 2013: onset, one year ahead",
              "Hindcast before 2013: occupancy", "Paddock-level onset AUC"),
  Supervised = c(scales::percent(state2_share[["Supervised"]], accuracy = 0.1), paste0(agreement_pct, "%"),
                 fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast")), fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast")),
                 fmt2(get_hindcast("Supervised", "occupancy", "hindcast")), fmt2(onset_skill$AUC[1])),
  Unsupervised = c(scales::percent(state2_share[["Unsupervised"]], accuracy = 0.1), "",
                   fmt2(get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset", "hindcast")), fmt2(get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast")),
                   fmt2(get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "occupancy", "hindcast")), fmt2(onset_skill$AUC[2]))
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

The anchors align the second state with mapped plague, which the paddock-level onset AUC (measured against those anchors) reflects. On the independent pre-2013 records, the two models are closer: `r if (get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset", "hindcast") > get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast")) "the unsupervised model scores higher on same-year onset and occupancy" else "the supervised model scores higher on same-year onset"`, `r if (get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast") > get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast")) "while the supervised model gives the better one-year-ahead warning" else "and the unsupervised model also gives the better one-year-ahead warning"`.

## Current forecast

**The maps below forecast `r forecast$target_season` `r forecast$target_year`**, from `r forecast$covariate_season` `r forecast$covariate_year` covariates (layer `r forecast$period`). Maps cover the prediction region: the fitted AE zones cut to SA2 cropping land plus 25 km around every surveyed paddock, so non-cropping parts of the zones (rangeland, forest, towns) aren't extrapolated to (`r/d_build_prediction_region.R`). The forecast reaches one season ahead only: every covariate is built from observed data, and each season's covariates set the transition into the following season.

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Pr(not-plague → plague) for ", forecast$target_season, " ", forecast$target_year, " at each 0.1 degree cell of the prediction region (cropping land within the fitted zones, plus 25 km around surveyed paddocks). Square-root colour scale (most cells are low risk). Supervised model left, unsupervised right.")
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.4

risk_scale <- scale_fill_gradientn(colors = hazard_colors, limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                                   breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1), trans = "sqrt", name = "Plague onset risk")
risk_maps <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  df <- as.data.frame(m$risk_map, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "risk"
  risk_tile_map(df, "risk", label, risk_scale)
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(risk_maps, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-risk-zones

risk_by_zone |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = c(mean, q90, max), names_sep = " | ") |>
  arrange(desc(`mean | Supervised`)) |>
  rename(`AE zone` = ae_zone) |>
```

### Nowcast from the latest month

The map above changes only at season boundaries (February, May, August, November), because GPP and soil moisture are season-end values. The nowcast reads every covariate at the latest complete month (`r nowcast$period`, against `r forecast$period` above), forecasting `r nowcast$target_season` `r nowcast$target_year`. It has no uncertainty map.

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-nowcast
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Nowcast of Pr(not-plague → plague) using covariates at ", nowcast$period, ". Same scale as the forecast map.")
#| fig-width: 12

  df <- as.data.frame(m$risk_map_nowcast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "risk"
  risk_tile_map(df, "risk", label, risk_scale)
})
```

### Uncertainty

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-uncertainty
#| fig-cap: "Width of the 95% interval for the forecast map, on the logit scale (a probability-scale width looks small whenever risk is near 0% or 100%, however uncertain the estimate). From 500 posterior draws of each model's coefficients. Darker = less certain."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.4

.logit <- function(p) log(p / (1 - p))
uncertainty_dfs <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  width <- .logit(m$risk_map_uncertainty[["ucl"]]) - .logit(m$risk_map_uncertainty[["lcl"]])
  df <- as.data.frame(width, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "logit_width"
  df
})
uncertainty_scale <- scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Purples", direction = 1,
                                          limits = range(unlist(lapply(uncertainty_dfs, `[[`, "logit_width"))),
                                          name = "95% interval width (logit)")
uncertainty_maps <- purrr::imap(uncertainty_dfs, function(df, label) risk_tile_map(df, "logit_width", label, uncertainty_scale))
patchwork::wrap_plots(uncertainty_maps, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Supervised model: median interval width `r fmt2(median(uncertainty_dfs$Supervised$logit_width))` logit units, widest `r fmt2(max(uncertainty_dfs$Supervised$logit_width))`.

### Covariates behind the forecast

```{r}
#| label: fig-predictor-maps
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Three of the transition covariates at ", forecast$period, " -- the grid, its AE-zone mean and its GRDC-subregion mean. Colour limits span each covariate's full record, so colours are comparable between forecasts.")
#| fig-width: 12

predictor_stacks <- list(
  `Rainfall whiplash`     = rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak,

  lapply(terra::mask, mask = terra::vect(fit_zones_ll))
predictor_rasters <- lapply(predictor_stacks, `[[`, forecast$period)
predictor_limits <- lapply(predictor_stacks, function(s) {
  rng <- terra::global(s, "range", na.rm = TRUE)
  c(min(rng$min, na.rm = TRUE), max(rng$max, na.rm = TRUE))
})

## Whiplash and the soil-moisture anomaly are z-scores, so a diverging scale with white at 0; GPP is
## always positive, so a sequential scale.
diverging <- function(label, low, high, title) {
  lim <- predictor_limits[[label]]
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c(low, "white", high), values = c(0, scales::rescale(0, from = lim), 1),
                       limits = lim, name = title, guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
}
predictor_scales <- list(
  `Rainfall whiplash`     = diverging("Rainfall whiplash", "#2166AC", "#B2182B", "Rainfall whiplash (z-score)"),
  `GPP (6-month rolling)` = scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = predictor_limits[["GPP (6-month rolling)"]], name = "GPP (gC/m²/day)",
                                                 guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)),
  `Soil moisture anomaly` = diverging("Soil moisture anomaly", "#8C510A", "#01665E", "Soil moisture anomaly (z-score)")
)

map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"), legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
map_coords <- coord_sf(xlim = c(zones_bbox["xmin"], zones_bbox["xmax"]),
                       ylim = c(zones_bbox["ymin"], zones_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE)

predictor_maps <- purrr::imap(predictor_rasters, function(r, label) {
  df <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "value"
  zone_sf <- mutate(fit_zones_ll, value = terra::extract(r, terra::vect(fit_zones_ll), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]])
  sub_sf <- mutate(grdc_subregion_ll, value = terra::extract(r, terra::vect(grdc_subregion_ll), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(value))
  outline <- geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6)
  list(
    ggplot() + geom_tile(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
      geom_sf(data = fit_zones_ll, fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) + outline + map_coords +
      labs(title = label) + map_theme + predictor_scales[[label]],
    ggplot() + geom_sf(data = zone_sf, aes(fill = value), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) + outline + map_coords +
      labs(title = paste(label, "- AE zone mean")) + map_theme + predictor_scales[[label]],
    ggplot() + geom_sf(data = sub_sf, aes(fill = value), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) + outline + map_coords +
      labs(title = paste(label, "- GRDC subregion mean")) + map_theme + predictor_scales[[label]]
  )
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(purrr::flatten(predictor_maps), ncol = 3)
```

## Limitations

```{r}
#| label: limitations-stats

## Near-singular joint precision (from collinear terms) makes the uncertainty sampling fall back to a
## generalised inverse; reported only if it occurs.
cond_numbers <- sapply(model_variants, function(m) {
  ev <- eigen(as.matrix(m$hmm$tmb_rep()$jointPrecision), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  max(ev) / min(ev)
})
```

- **Few independent plague events.** The plague transition rests on `r nrow(mapped_seasons)` mapped plague seasons; it improves only as more seasons are mapped.
- **One season ahead.** The covariates are observed data, so the forecast cannot extend beyond the season after the latest complete covariate period.
- **Coarse validation before 2013.** The hindcast is scored against state-by-year records with no WA coverage, and no anchors exist before `r first_mapped_year`.
- **Weak warning for some plagues.** Onset risk rises well ahead of the 2010-11 plague but only weakly ahead of the 2020-21 NSW plague (@fig-hindcast-timeseries), a limit of the current covariates.
- **Imperfect count distributions.** `r if (length(ppc_outside) > 0) paste0("Simulated data miss the ", and_join(ppc_label(ppc_outside)), " (Model checks), so the count families don't capture every feature of the data.") else "Simulated data match the checked statistics (Model checks)."`
- **Survey grids sharing coordinates.** Some sites surveyed two grids or transects on the same dates under one set of coordinates (e.g. crop and pasture pairs); cleaning keeps one of each pair, which can favour the busier grid (`r/a_clean_deduplicate_surveys.R`).
- **Patched hmmTMB.** The beta-binomial family comes from a patched hmmTMB (github.com/matt-w-rees/hmmTMB, pinned in `renv.lock`); upstream fixes arrive only when merged into it.
- `r if (any(cond_numbers > 1e12)) paste0("**Near-singular precision matrix** (condition number ", formatC(max(cond_numbers), format = "e", digits = 1), "): the uncertainty sampling falls back to a generalised inverse, which can understate interval widths along the affected directions.") else "**Uncertainty sampling** uses a well-conditioned precision matrix in both models."`
